html:
The Ngarigo are an Aboriginal people of the high country of southeast New South Wales, on the Monaro plains and in the Snowy Mountains, reaching across the border into Victoria.

Each summer peoples from a wide area climbed into the mountains to feast on bogong moths, which gather in their millions in rock crevices on the peaks. The moths were roasted and eaten, and the gatherings were also times for ceremony, trade and marriage. Neighbours on the map include the Ngunawal to the north, the Yuin on the coast, the Jaitmatang to the southwest and the Gunaikurnai to the south.

Squatters spread across the Monaro in the 1820s and 1830s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Ngarigo are an Aboriginal people of the high country of southeast New South Wales, on the Monaro plains and in the Snowy Mountains, reaching across the border into Victoria.
